done_when: Before sign-off in a client repo, ready prototype fixes merge by the agent; one install script sets up a Mac for prototyping; the skill tells the agent to batch changes per demo round, speak in demo terms and say when to connect the deploy platform; a start-a-prototype checklist exists

findings.body: The checklist sends a fresh user to `forge init` without signing the GitHub CLI in. The unchanged README names `gh auth login` as a prerequisite (README.md:113), and `forge init` commits and pushes before calling `gh api` to protect the branch (src/forge/init.py:221-228). Without CLI authentication, setup fails after the first commit; rerunning `forge init` then refuses because the repo already has commits (src/forge/init.py:205-208). Add the login step before init and give a recovery action for this failure.
findings.title: Not done: A checklist starts a prototype

findings.body: The decision says `forge next` tells the agent to merge unsigned prototype work, but src/forge/nextstep.py:304 and :317 still read the raw `merge` setting. With `merge = "human"`, it recommends a human merge even though `forge close` recommends `forge merge`. The agent skill also still says a human merges by default (src/forge/templates/skill.md:41-43). The story assigns these changes to TALK, so that task must land before this claim is true.
findings.title: Later: TALK must make forge next recommend agent merging

findings.body: The Mac one-liner here and the Windows one at line 22 target `scripts/install-mac.sh` and `scripts/install-windows.ps1`, but neither script exists in this checkout. A user following the published checklist cannot complete laptop setup yet. The story's Tasks table assigns both scripts and their test to INSTALL (plans/FORGE-SALES-1.md:68).
findings.title: Later: INSTALL must publish the checklist's scripts

why: Salespeople can run the FDE route but trip on the engineering around it: they would have to merge pull requests, set up Node, Docker and test browsers by hand, see each small tweak wait for a full review, and hear Forge's words instead of the demo's
